 'Como's development as a team is mirroring Cesc's as a manager' published at 22:44 GMT 22:44 GMT 
 FT: Lens 1-9 Como 
 Stephen Warnock 
Former Liverpool defender on MOTD: UEFA Champions League 
 Como are such an exciting team to watch but there is a balance as well. They know how to defend but, going forward they are so dangerous. 
 I think the big thing when you look at what they are doing is that, yes, they have got rich owners but that alone doesn't buy you guaranteed success - you have got to buy the right players to fit the right system and Cesc Fabregas has gone for young players as well who are hungry but also can keep progressing and keep improving, like he is as a manager.
 So the team's development is almost mirroring his development, in the way that they are going to progress together. It's a brilliant story.

 Some more stats from Como's 9-1 win at Lens if you'd indulge us.
 Como have equalled the
 most goals scored by any club in their first four major European matches
 (19), matching Queens Park Rangers in 1976. They have surpassed the Champions League record by five goals, previously held by Juventus (14 in
 1995-96).
 Lens have suffered the
 joint-heaviest defeat by a French club in major European competition,
 alongside Strasbourg’s 10-2 loss at MTK Budapest in 1961. No French side
 had previously lost a major European home match by more than five goals.
 Como are only the second
 club to score nine goals in a UEFA Champions League match, after Bayern
 München vs Dinamo Zagreb in September 2024 (9-2). They are the first
 Italian side to score nine in major European competition since Roma beat
 Altay SK 10-1 in 1962.
 Como are the first side
 to have 11 different players score or assist in a UEFA Champions League
 match, overtaking the previous record of 10 set by Benfica in their 6-1
 win against Maccabi Haifa in November 2022.

 'Strange goal to concede for such a brilliant goalkeeper' published at 22:34 GMT 22:34 GMT 
 FT: RB Leipzig 2-3 Man City 
 Owen Hargreaves 
Former Manchester United midfielder on TNT Sports 
 I think it was a cross [Baku goal], but obviously it nestles into the net and for all players at the top you get punished if you make mistakes. 
 You have to hope for the best and plan for the worst and [Gianluigi Donnarumma] doesn't really need to be there, and be that far off his line because if he's a yard back he just picks the ball up quite easily. 
 He probably just didn't get back in the position that he anticipated, he probably thought he was closer to the goal than he was, but strange goal to concede for such a brilliant goalkeeper.

 'A lot to learn' published at 22:31 GMT 22:31 GMT 
 FT: Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Image source, Getty Images Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to TNT Sports: "Always we need to value winning away in the Champions League. It is extremely difficult. Two very different halves. We should have had three or four goals in the first half but we didn't do it. Right at the start of the second half we were on the back foot, very sloppy and gave balls away. Then we had to suffer. A lot to learn.
 "We should have scored more in the first half and if we didn't do that we had to go and do that in the second half.
 "We made six changes but we know the quality of the players we have. Whether we were lacking something I don't know but I would have done the same thing [again].
 "I value what the team has done now, it is 11 away games we played."

Former Liverpool midfielder on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 On Gianluigi Donnarumma's performances: 
 There were moments again like that goal against PSG when Manchester City were about to get momentum in the game and he threw one in. Tonight I thought he should do better at the near post [for the first RB Leipzig goal]. There was a shot in the first half that nearly goes in.  'Second half was completely different' published at 22:20 GMT 22:20 GMT 
 FT: Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Image source, Getty Images Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya, speaking to TNT Sports: "First half we played really, really well. We created a lot of chances and could have scored more but the second half was completely different. They stepped up a gear and made it difficult for us and we have to learn from it. Delighted with the win but a lot of things to improve going forward.
 "Maybe they started pressing a bit higher with more intensity. We had too many giveaways especially in the final third. There was too much running from box to box and we have to manage those reactions and go for the third and fourth goal.
 "At the end of the day it is three points."

 'We need to step up a bit' published at 22:17 GMT 22:17 GMT 
 FT: RB Leipzig 2-3 Man City 
 Manchester City 
 Manchester City striker Erling Haaland speaking to TNT Sports about being ready when chances come: "Not sure how many touches I had today, not the most but what is the most important is that I managed to help the team to win. I think we need to step up a bit, when we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third - that's what we have to do. We have to work on that."
 What improvements? "Keeping the ball, when to keep it when to go, working together offensively and defensively. You can always be better and there's always a new chance. A new game in three days so that's lovely."
 On being ready for chances: "You can look at it that it's difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it's only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance - you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option."

 By Alex Howell Football reporter Viktor Gyokeres scored and provided an assist as Arsenal continued their unbeaten start in the league phase of the Champions League with a win over Slavia Prague. 
 Manager Mikel Arteta made six changes to the team that beat Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, with Gyokeres leading the line in place of Kai Havertz.
 The Swedish striker played a huge part in the opening goal when he hooked the ball behind the Slavia Prague defence for Noni Madueke to race on to and finish confidently in the ninth minute.
 Gyokeres added the second himself before half-time after he exchanged passes with Mikel Merino and curled an excellent finish in off the post.
 Slavia Prague improved after the break, and almost immediately David Raya had to produce a good save to deny Oskar Kubiak who shot from the edge of the box.
 Gabriel Magalhaes had to clear the ball off the line after a Mojmir Chytil header following a corner, and the home side eventually pulled one back when Wiktor Nowak scored from close range in the 90th minute.
 The Gunners, who had a 100% record in this stage of the competition during the last campaign, are unbeaten after their opening four games this season and are third in the table behind Paris St-Germain and Real Madrid.
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Viktor Gyokeres scored and assisted as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague
 Arsenal player ratings 
 Arsenal starting XI: 
 David Raya: Raya had to make a smart stop in the opening minute of the second half but flapped at a corner which resulted in the ball being cleared off the line. 6 
 Ben White: The full-back was very comfortable when dealing with the Slavia attacks. 7 
 Ezri Konsa: A decent night for Konsa but gave away a free-kick on the edge of the box and was booked for a late challenge in the second half. 6 
 Gabriel Magalhaes: The usual dependable performance from the centre-back. A clearance off the line in the second half. 7 
 Piero Hincapie: Aggressive defending from Hincapie and his overlapping runs created space for Eberechi Eze. 7 
 Martin Zubimendi: Just Zubimendi's third start of the season. Tidy in possession but looks like he still needs more minutes to be at his best. 6 
 Declan Rice: Captained the team and continued his excellent start to the season with a dominant display. 8 
 Mikel Merino: The Spaniard played close to striker Gyokeres and was a threat in the box. 7 
 Noni Madueke: The winger has started to look like he is playing himself into form and carried that on against Slavia Prague. Lots of direct running and a good finish for the opening goal. 7 
 Eberechi Eze: Some bright moments in the first half and came in-field when he had the ball to link up with the rest of the Arsenal attack. 6 
 Viktor Gyokeres: A really good night for the striker who needed a good performance. Gyokeres held up play, created the opening goal and scored the second. 8 
 Substitutes: 
 Cristhian Mosquera (on 62, Konsa): A good half an hour for the young defender. 6 
 Christos Tzolis (on 62, Eze): The winger was not involved in a lot after coming on. 6 
 Jurrien Timber (on 78, White): Replaced White as Arsenal saw out the win. 6 
 Martin Odegaard (on 78 Gyokeres): Added his usual energy to midfield. 6 
 Dowman (on 90, Madueke) 
 Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, Meslier, Saliba, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly.
